topics.label: Lecture introduction and objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening section introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the key learning objectives regarding the causes of cancer.

topics.label: Cancer etiology and the balance of genetics, environment, and chance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational drivers of cancer development by examining how genetic predisposition, endogenous random mutations, and environmental exposures interact across populations.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how biological infectious agents drive oncogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study of pathogen-driven malignancy.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how specific chemical and physical agents cause direct or indirect DNA damage, including their requirements for metabolic activation and tissue-specific processing.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, host susceptibility, and mechanistic summary
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic factors that facilitate cancer outgrowth, including promotional stimuli, host developmental windows, and an integrated summary of carcinogenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Methods for identifying carcinogens and evaluating cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the genomic, epidemiological, and experimental methodologies used to prove carcinogenicity and evaluate practical exposure risks.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This closing section summarises the key takeaways of the lecture and brings the presentation to a conclusion.
